question: A $150\times 324\times 375$ rectangular solid is made by gluing together $1\times 1\times 1$ cubes. An internal diagonal of this solid passes through the interiors of how many of the $1\times 1\times 1$ cubes?
solution:
Parameterize the diagonal by (150t, 324t, 375t) for 0 ≤ t ≤ 1. It starts in one cube and enters one new cube at each distinct interior time when any coordinate is an integer, even if several coordinates become integers together.

For a side of length d, the crossing times are k/d for 1 ≤ k < d. For sides d and e, a time is shared exactly when its reduced denominator divides both d and e, so there are gcd(d,e) − 1 shared interior times. The same reasoning applies to all three sides. The pairwise gcds are gcd(150,324) = 6, gcd(150,375) = 75, and gcd(324,375) = 3; the triple gcd is 3.

By inclusion-exclusion, adding the starting cube to the count of distinct crossings gives 1 + (149 + 323 + 374) − (5 + 74 + 2) + 2 = 768 cubes.
Final answer: 768
